steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

steps.message:
Analysis: Current inspect omits migration_flags and decodes slice_ns incorrectly for both captures. The route map identifies the three required repair files, while field_emit is the consumer of generated offsets. Removing synctab_out caused current synctab to fail immediately because it does not create the output directory; no guard was written, which is correct for failure. We now need read all pipeline code, format/rules, live release, and binary capture bytes to determine intended fixes.
Plan: Inspect the Makefile and every relevant C/header/rule file with line numbers. Examine existing layout/provenance behavior after recreating the output directory, inspect available live/bundle layout inputs and release data, and dump capture bytes. This should expose deliberately incorrect input selection, writer, provenance gate, and possibly field emission logic.

arguments.keystrokes: printf '%s\n' '--- Makefile ---'; nl -ba /app/lagpipe/Makefile; for f in /app/relc/input.c /app/lagpipe/tblw/emit_writer.c /app/lagpipe/tagc/gate.c /app/lagpipe/tagc/gate.h /app/lagpipe/synclink/common.h /app/lagpipe/synclink/driver.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/parse_layout.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/field_emit.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/rebuild.c; do echo "--- $f ---"; nl -ba "$f"; done

for f in /app/lagpipe/fieldnotes/FIELD_RULES.txt /app/lagpipe/synclink/ARCHITECTURE /app/lagpipe/BUILDCHANNEL /app/lagpipe/VERIFIER_CHANNEL /app/memvault/MANIFEST /app/memvault/regression/bundle_pick_input.c; do echo "--- $f ---"; nl -ba "$f"; done; echo '--- livekern tree ---'; find /app/livekern -maxdepth 3 -type f -printf '%p\n' -exec sh -c 'echo CONTENT:; sed -n "1,80p" "$1"' _ {} \; 2>/dev/null

echo '--- other likely inputs/artifacts ---'; find /app -maxdepth 4 -type f \( -iname '*layout*' -o -iname '*release*' -o -iname '*bundle*' -o -iname '*.tbl' -o -iname '*.tag' \) -printf '%p\n' | sort; echo '--- captures hex ---'; for f in /app/memvault/samples/*.mem; do echo "$f"; xxd -g1 "$f"; done
mkdir -p /app/lagpipe/synctab_out; /app/bin/kernscribe synctab; rc=$?; echo "SYNCTAB_RC=$rc"; find /app/lagpipe/synctab_out -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf '%f: ' -exec cat {} \; -printf '\n'; true

steps.message:
Analysis: The live export already contains the correct four-field layout: pid@0, weight@4, migration_flags@8, slice_ns@12. Existing synctab instead selects a bundled snapshot and succeeds because gate.c accepts every tag, producing the observed three-field stale layout. The required fixes are therefore to choose the live export and emit live provenance, reject bundle tags, and ensure writer validation does not leave an accepted output on a forbidden origin. We still need the untruncated driver/rebuild code to confirm offline_guard semantics and inspect bounds behavior.
Plan: Read the omitted source units and inspect exact capture sizes/bytes using od. Then patch the three route-map modules: input.c will read and trim running.release and select /app/livekern/exports/sched_entity.tab with live provenance; gate.c will only accept live tags and reject bundle origins; emit_writer.c will validate provenance before publishing layout and use a temporary file/cleanup to avoid partial success artifacts. If driver lacks correct guard/failure cleanup, adjust the writer behavior where possible and inspect whether driver changes are necessary.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in /app/lagpipe/synclink/driver.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/parse_layout.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/field_emit.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/rebuild.c /app/lagpipe/synclink/common.h; do echo "--- $f ---"; cat "$f"; done

echo '--- snapvault ---'; find /app/snapvault -maxdepth 4 -type f -printf '%p\n' -exec sh -c 'sed -n "1,80p" "$1"' _ {} \; 2>/dev/null; echo '--- capture bytes ---'; for f in /app/memvault/samples/*.mem; do echo "$f ($(stat -c %s "$f") bytes)"; od -An -tx1 -v "$f"; done

steps.message:
Analysis: The intended live layout exactly matches the 20-byte captures and reference values. Synctab also lacks the required offline_guard lifecycle: driver.c never creates it and does not clean outputs on failure. A robust repair needs the three mapped modules plus driver orchestration so forbidden bundle origins cannot leave provenance/layout/guard artifacts, and successful rebuilds stamp offline_guard.ok.
Plan: Replace input selection with the live export and trimmed running release, implement strict live-only provenance acceptance, make layout publication atomic and validate the tag before writing, and update driver.c to remove stale outputs at start/failure and write offline_guard.ok=1 only after layout generation and ELF rebuild succeed. Then run the mandated make bind and synctab, compare every inspect result byte-for-byte with its reference, and inspect generated artifacts.
